_note: ROUND 2 BRIEFS. Each entry is the ENTIRE input the planner gets: category + natural-language brief only. r01-europa.brief: NASA's Europa Clipper is flying to an ice-covered moon with a hidden ocean. Make space nerds feel the anticipation.

r02-blue-hour.brief: Teaser for Blue Hour, a late-night jazz trio's new album. Make someone who never listens to jazz press play.

r03-brutalism.brief: Defend Brutalist concrete architecture to people who think it's ugly. Change one mind.

r04-hangul.brief: Tell the story of King Sejong inventing the Korean alphabet so commoners could read. A history short for curious teens.

r05-sleep.brief: Explain why the first half of the night matters most for deep sleep. A health short for chronic scrollers.

r06-wolves.brief: Yellowstone brought wolves back and the rivers changed. Make the case for rewilding to skeptics.

r07-shutdown.brief: A founder shut down her startup after three years. Turn the postmortem into the most useful seconds of another founder's week.

r08-final-move.brief: World championship, final game, one move decides everything. Make non-chess fans feel the tension.

r09-dreams.brief: Why do we dream? Answer it for an eight-year-old — scientifically true, but magical.

r10-capsule.brief: Five pieces, thirty outfits. Convince a maximalist to try a capsule wardrobe.

r11-cabin.brief: An off-grid cabin in the pines, no road access in winter. Find it the right buyer, not the most buyers.

r12-plastic.brief: Eight million tons of plastic enter the ocean every year. Turn guilt into one concrete action.

r13-permadeath.brief: An indie roguelike where you die every ten minutes — on purpose. Hype the launch for skeptical scrollers.

r14-theseus.brief: If every plank of a ship is replaced, is it still the same ship? A teaser that starts arguments.

r15-skyborn.brief: What did the sky look like the day you were born? Invite someone to find their birth sky.
